verses: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying,
Let the children of Israel also keep the Passover at his appointed season.
On the fourteenth day of this month, at evening, you must keep it at his appointed season; according to all its rites and all its ceremonies, you must keep it.
Moses spoke to the children of Israel, that they should keep the Passover.
They kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month at evening in the wilderness of Sinai: according to all that the LORD commanded Moses, the children of Israel did so.
# Certain men were defiled by the dead body of a man, so they could not keep the Passover that day; they came before Moses and Aaron that day:
Those men said to him, "We are defiled by the dead body of a man; why are we kept back, that we may not offer an offering of the LORD at his appointed season among the children of Israel?"
Moses said to them, "Stand still, and I will hear what the LORD will command concerning you."
# The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
Speak to the children of Israel, saying, 'If any man among you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead body, or is on a distant journey, he must still keep the Passover to the LORD.'
On the fourteenth day of the second month at evening they must keep it, and eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They must leave none of it until morning, nor break any bone of it: according to all the ordinances of the Passover they must keep it.

But the man who is clean, and is not on a journey, and refrains from keeping the Passover, that same person will be cut off from among his people, because he did not bring the offering of the LORD at his appointed season; that man will bear his sin.

If a stranger lives among you and keeps the Passover to the LORD, according to the ordinance of the Passover and according to its manner, so he must do; you must have one ordinance, both for the stranger and for the native-born.
# And on the day the tabernacle was erected, a cloud covered the tabernacle, that is, the tent of the testimony; and in the evening there was on the tabernacle what looked like fire, until morning.
Thus it was always: the cloud covered it by day, and fire appeared by night.
When the cloud was lifted from the tabernacle, the children of Israel then journeyed; and in the place where the cloud stayed, the children of Israel pitched their tents.
By the LORD's command the children of Israel journeyed, and by the LORD's command they pitched; as long as the cloud stayed over the tabernacle they rested in their tents.
When the cloud lingered long over the tabernacle for many days, the children of Israel kept the LORD's command and did not journey.
And so it was: when the cloud was over the tabernacle for a few days, by the LORD's command they stayed in their tents, and by the LORD's command they journeyed.
And so it was: when the cloud stayed from evening until morning, and the cloud was lifted in the morning, they journeyed; whether the cloud was lifted by day or by night, they journeyed.

Whether it was two days, a month, or a year that the cloud lingered over the tabernacle, remaining there, the children of Israel stayed in their tents and did not journey; but when it was lifted, they journeyed.
By the LORD's command they rested in the tents, and by the LORD's command they journeyed; they kept the LORD's command, by the LORD's command through the hand of Moses.
